question_text: A 23-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of pain during intercourse and vaginal dryness. The patient has also had intermittent hot flashes and fatigue during this time. Over the past year, her periods have become irregular. Her last menstrual period was over six months ago. She is sexually active with one partner and does not use protection or contraception. She has a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia during childhood, which has remained in remission. Pelvic examination shows an atrophic cervix and vagina. A urinary pregnancy test is negative. A progestin challenge test is performed and shows no withdrawal bleeding. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?
